Corollary
[almost nonnegative curvature] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0046 ↗ thm:chow-ii-hamilton-ivey 1. ch10:10.19\group Ricci-flow applications

For a normalized three-dimensional flow with $\nu (\cdot ,0)\ge -1$, there is a bounded nonincreasing function $\phi $ with $\phi (s)\to 0$ as $s\to \infty $ such that \[ \Rm \ge -\phi (R)R-3e^6, \] and, wherever $R\ge 3e^6$, the additive constant may be omitted.
Proof

\sketch Set $\psi (s)=s(\log s-3)$ on $(e^3,\infty )$ and let $\psi ^{-1}$ be its inverse. The Hamilton–Ivey inequality gives the assertion with $\phi (s)=\psi ^{-1}(s)/s$ above $3e^6$ and $\phi =0$ below it. Monotonicity and the limit follow by differentiating $\psi $.

□
